born.why: The code prioritizes survival by eating known-safe fruits immediately when hungry, tasting novel or ambiguous fruits to build a safety diary, and avoiding poisonous history unless starving, while preventing double-carrying.

The code improves survival by leveraging trait-based similarity to known safe fruits (allowing transfer of safety knowledge between species) and prioritizing carrying when hunger is low to build a pantry, while using taste tests for novel/uncertain fruits unless starvation forces immediate eating.

The code prioritizes survival by strictly avoiding fruits with a history of harm unless starving, uses tasting to resolve uncertainty for novel or mixed-history fruits, and leverages innate preferences only when data is lacking or hunger is critical.

The code prioritizes survival by distinguishing "safe" from "poisonous" via majority vote in the diary, avoids eating confirmed poison even when starving unless desperate, carries safe food home to reduce future foraging costs, and only tastes unknown fruits when hunger is manageable to gather data without risking death.

The code prioritizes safety by requiring more evidence (2+ samples, >80% safe ratio) before switching to 'eat', preventing early deaths from false positives on novel fruits. It only gambles on 'eat' when starvation is imminent (>90 hunger), otherwise defaults to 'taste' for uncertain fruits to gather data without high risk, ensuring long-term survival through better learning.

It prioritizes safety by tracking species and trait-clones (color/smell) to avoid repeating mistakes, uses heuristics (sweet smell) to reduce blind tasting, and escalates to desperate eating only at extreme starvation levels.
